label: Revision-authored AQA-style practice question (original, not an AQA question)

question.context: Revision-authored AQA-style practice. A café wants to improve operating profit. Management proposes raising menu prices by 15%, while competitors' prices remain unchanged. Customers may be price-sensitive.
question.stem: Which evaluation best reflects the uncertainty in the proposed profitability improvement?

options.label: A
options.text: A 15% price rise guarantees a 15% increase in operating profit even if sales volume falls.

options.label: B
options.text: Higher prices always improve profit margins and total profit regardless of customers' response.

options.label: C
options.text: A price rise can increase contribution per item, but a sufficient fall in sales volume could reduce total contribution and profit.

options.label: D
options.text: Changing selling price has no effect on revenue or contribution, only on fixed costs.

option_rationale: A is incorrect because operating profit depends on price, quantity and costs; volume may fall.
B is incorrect because a higher per-item margin does not guarantee higher total profit.
C is correct because the effect depends on demand responsiveness, competitive position and contribution lost from any reduction in sales volume.
D is incorrect because price directly changes revenue and contribution per unit under a simple variable-cost assumption.
mark_scheme.model_answer: C. Test demand response and total contribution, not only the higher price per item; pricing is a trade-off rather than an automatic improvement.
